join_order.notes: Iterate 8 target k_ids; CSR yields mk row ids; load mk_movie_id[mk_row] to get t_id.
production_year_bin[t_id-1] > 2000 && != INT32_MIN. Dedup t_ids per k_id to avoid repeated ci probes.

join_order.probe: cast_info via offsets idx cast_info__movie_id, scan person_id[lo..hi]
join_order.notes: downey_robert_ids tiny; use sorted std::array linear scan or 2-element compare; avoid hash overhead.

data_structures.downey_robert_ids: std::vector<int32_t> (size ~2, sorted) for linear membership test
data_structures.t_id_dedup_per_k: std::vector<uint8_t> seen_t bitset(2528312) OR per-k_id local dedup; bitset shared across k_ids to dedup globally for ci probe efficiency
data_structures.k_id_to_t_witness: track which k_ids contributed a surviving tuple for MIN(k.keyword)
data_structures.min_aggregates: three int32_t row-id witnesses (k_id, n_id, t_id) yielding lexicographic MIN via varlen compare; final varlen resolution at end

parallelism.notes: 8 k_ids drive small mk fan-out; year-filtered t_ids then drive ci probes. ci probe is the dominant cost (~37M rows total but constrained by t_id ranges). Use single-threaded execution: per-k_id work is tiny, parallelism overhead > benefit. Year>2000 keeps ~33% of titles so ci probe range remains moderate.

output.notes: Scalar aggregate; no GROUP BY. Resolve varlen strings only for final witness rows (or compare-as-you-go via varlen reads).

execution_steps: 1. Memory-map keyword.off/keyword.dat; scan 134170 rows; for each, check membership in 8-literal set; collect target_k_ids (~8).
2. Memory-map name.off/name.dat; scan 4167491 rows; substring test for 'Downey' then 'Robert' (or single LIKE matcher); collect downey_robert_ids (~2).
3. Load mk_off (134172), mk_rowids (4523930), mk_movie_id (4523930), production_year (2528312), ci_off (2528314), ci_person_id (36244344).
4. Allocate seen_t bitset of 2528312 bits to dedup t_ids across k_ids (avoid duplicate ci probes when multiple k_ids share a movie).

5. For each k_id in target_k_ids: walk CSR [mk_off[k_id], mk_off[k_id+1]); for each mk_row, t_id = mk_movie_id[mk_row]; if !seen_t[t_id] && production_year[t_id-1] > 2000 && production_year[t_id-1] != INT32_MIN, set seen_t and probe ci_off[t_id]..ci_off[t_id+1]; for each ci row, check ci_person_id[r] in downey_robert_ids (linear over 2 elements); on match, update three MIN witnesses (k_id, n_id, t_id) by lexicographic varlen compare.
6. After loop, materialize three MIN varlen strings via .off/.dat reads of winning row ids and emit.
